event.description: @ Join us in Downtown Miami at MDC Wolfson Campus! Doors open at 11:00 am for complimentary coffee for the first 50 participants Join the Museum of Miami for an afternoon of connection and dialogue at la ventanita! Facilitated by community leaders, educators, and artists, conversations will be guided by prompts surrounding themes of history, culture, and identity—all inspired by our communities. Listen and share stories while engaging together over coffee. Spark your civic interest and explore the ways in which you can inspire meaningful change in your community! Connect with Maydee Martinez, the youngest founding member of Engage Miami and former Teen Miami Intern Curator at Museum of Miami. Follow Maydee’s journey to becoming a leader in civic engagement, youth development, and community organizing. Learn how active participation by Miamians can lead to lasting change. This program will encourage exchange around navigating civic issues in our communities as we look towards Miami’s future. Enjoy a free coffee on us! Complimentary coffee available to the first 50 participants at check-in. Coffee provided by Cienfuegos Coffee. This program will take place at Miami Dade College — Wolfson Campus, Building 2, Room 2106, located at 223 NE 4th St, Miami, FL 33132. Coffee provided by Cienfuegos Coffee. The Miami Stories Recording Booth Share your story with us at our portable recording booth. Participants will record an audio interview which will be preserved in the museum’s archive. Hands on History Engage with objects from the museum’s education collection inspired by Miami’s history! noon Cafecito Conversations—Youth Voices & Miami’s Future featuring Maydee Martinez 12:45 p.m. Miami Stories Activity – Story Dice Game 1:30 p.m. Program Ends *Program schedule is subject to change Featured Speaker: A person with shoulder length brown hair wearing a structured cream blazer, black blouse, silver watch, and small enamel pin smiles at the camera against a beige background. Maydee Martinez Maydee Martinez was proudly born and raised in Miami, Florida, and has dedicated her career to community engagement and civic education. She began her professional career at the Museum of Miami as a Teen Miami Intern Curator and went on to graduate from Miami Dade College’s Honors College and Georgetown University, where she earned a B.A. in Sociology and Government and researched civic participation among Hispanic/Latino youth in South Florida. In 2014, Maydee founded Democracy YOUnited, a voter education and engagement initiative, and later helped launch Engage Miami, a nonprofit focused on changing the culture around local politics. She has worked on political campaigns throughout South Florida, having last served as Political Director for now-Miami-Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava in 2020. She also curated Vote the Future, a youth civic education program that employed more than 120 high school students. Today, Maydee serves as Director of Miami-Dade Initiatives at Hispanic Unity of Florida, where she works to expand access to programs that help individuals and families become self-sufficient, civically engaged, and achieve the American Dream Moderator: Caroline Klibanoff Caroline Klibanoff is the Executive Director of Made By Us, a nationwide nonprofit activating 500+ museums, historic sites, libraries, and archives as trusted bridges to active citizenship for teens and young adults. Under her direction, Made By Us has reached 85 million Americans, built an annual Civic Season between Juneteenth and July 4th, launched the nation’s first-ever national youth bureau for the U.S. 250th anniversary, and transferred $1 million directly to youth contributors shaping that milestone. A keynote speaker at TED, AdWeek, SXSW, and the American Alliance of Museums, and quoted in the Wall Street Journal, The New Yorker, and the AP, she is an Eisenhower USA Fellow, a Smithsonian Research Associate, a board member of the Public Education Project, and a juror on the inaugural David Rubenstein Prize for American History. event.description: @ Celebrate spooky season with a visit to Miami City Cemetery! Families are invited to meet Julia Tuttle and early notable Miamians as you engage with history. Hear stories of how the Magic City came to be and of the people who helped shape this community. Curated for families with children ages 7 and up. All are welcome to come as you are or in costume!* *Costumes and some costume masks may be worn; masks must provide unobstructed peripheral vision at all times with openings that allow the eyes to be fully seen. Costumes must be family friendly. Costumes may not contain sharp objects, pointed objects or materials that may accidentally strike another guest. Members: $25, Non-Members: $35, Children 14 & Under: $15 Register Featured Speaker: A person stands with their arms crossed in front of a large museum exhibition case with several rows of brown dire wolf skulls against an orange backdrop. Ingrid E. Argueta Coordinator of Education Programs and Community Engagement Ingrid E. Argueta was born in Guatemala and immigrated to Miami when she was 7 years old. Although not a native Miamian, she is a 305-er at heart. Ingrid has remained true to her indigenous roots and is passionate about Native American history and culture. She is best known for her eco-history tours of Miami’s historic sites, neighborhoods, and waterways. Ingrid currently serves as Museum of Miami’s Coordinator of Education Programs and Community Engagement and has been with the museum for over 10 years. Additional Information Please see below for additional information regarding the tour. For further assistance, please contact Visitor Services at (305) 375-1492 or email programs@museumofmiami.org. Helpful Tips We recommend bringing a water bottle, wearing light clothing, bug spray, and comfortable shoes for walking. Please bring a flashlight, as the cemetery will be dark after sunset. Restrooms are available onsite at the cemetery. All are welcome to come as you are or in costume! Wayfinding Upon arrival to the Miami City Cemetery, please check-in with Museum staff. The check-in table will be located near the Belcher crypt. Please enter the cemetery through the entrance on NE 2nd Avenue. Parking There is limited parking available inside the cemetery along the driveway. If you prefer to park outside of the cemetery, there is a lot just north of the cemetery, across the street from Temple Israel off NE 19th Street. event.title: City Tour—Annual Miami City Cemetery Walking Tour
event.description: @ Connect with the past on a walking tour of the Miami City Cemetery with Museum of Miami’s Coordinator of Education Programs and Community Engagement, Ingrid E. Argueta, and its Resident Historian, Dr. Paul S. George. Founded in 1897, just a year after the city’s incorporation, this historic graveyard is a monument to so many of the people who helped shape the early history of the Magic City. Hear stories of notable Miami residents, including civil rights leader Reverend Theodore Gibson, “Mother of Miami” Julia Tuttle, and Bernard Mackey of the Ink Spots Quartet. View the final resting place of Carrie B. Miller, whose body was encased in cement to preserve her sleeping form. All are welcome to come as you are or in costume! Members: $25, Non-Members: $35, Children 14 & Under: $15 Register A group of tour participants stand in a cemetery at night. They look on to two performers in historical costume. Jack-o-lanterns and candles light up the scene. Featured Speakers: Paul S. George, Ph.D. Resident Historian For over three decades, Museum of Miami’s Resident Historian Dr. Paul S. George has toured his way to local, national, and international acclaim with his continuing series of historic tours. Through walking, coach, and boat tour experiences, Dr. George has welcomed tour participants on a memorable journey of South Florida through its historic neighborhoods, landmarks, and sites. As a Miami native, author, and former college professor, Dr. George has gained fame for his uncanny ability to recall the most impressive details about the people and places that make South Florida so unique. Dr. George, wearing a blue pinstripe suit, burgundy striped tie, and white shirt stands in front of a gallery of black and white archival images against a gray wall. Argueta Coordinator of Education Programs and Community Engagement Ingrid E. Argueta was born in Guatemala and immigrated to Miami when she was 7 years old. Although not a native Miamian, she is a 305-er at heart. Ingrid has remained true to her indigenous roots and is passionate about Native American history and culture. She is best known for her eco-history tours of Miami’s historic sites, neighborhoods, and waterways. Ingrid currently serves as Museum of Miami’s Coordinator of Education Programs and Community Engagement and has been with the museum for over 10 years. Additional Information Please see below for additional information regarding the tour. For further assistance, please contact Visitor Services at (305) 375-1492 or email programs@museumofmiami.org. Helpful Tips Please plan on arriving to Bayside Marketplace between 6:15 pm and 6:45 pm for check-in. The tour may begin any time after 7:00 pm, so please be on time as Miami’s traffic may be unpredictable. Once the boat has left the dock, it will be unable to return for late tour participants. We suggest bringing water and wearing sun protection. Water and soda service will be provided onboard by Island Queen Cruises. Additional light snacks and drinks are available to purchase from Island Queen Cruises. Wayfinding We will be boarding a vessel from the Island Queen fleet, which will be docked at the marina at Bayside Marketplace. The Island Queen Cruises dock is located inside Bayside Marketplace through the main entrance. Walk past the flags and straight towards the back by the marina. Parking & Public Transit Parking at Bayside Marketplace: There is parking at the Bayside Marketplace parking garage between NE 4th and 5th streets. Alternate Parking: Nearby parking garages in Downtown Miami and metered parking are also available in the median on Biscayne Blvd. or in neighborhood lots across from Bayside Marketplace. Public Transportation: Should you wish to take public transportation, we suggest downloading the MDT Tracker App to view bus schedules or visiting https://www.miamidade.gov/transit/mobile/ to plan your trip. Bayside Marketplace is accessible by Metromover. Stop: College/Bayside. Charter Information View of a white vessel with the words, Island Queen’s Miami Lady is a large vessel with two decks. The lower deck is closed in and is air-conditioned. This level has tables and chairs for tour participants to sit in and speakers so that patrons may listen to the tour guide from below. Guests may also choose to stand on the bow or stern of the vessel on the lower level. The upper level is accessible by stairs only. The upper deck is covered on the top with open sides. Should there be rainy weather, there is plastic side sheeting, which may be rolled down. There are chairs for guests to use on this level. The tour guides on the vessel will stand in the front of the upper level for narration. Please note that the capacity of the vessel is 140 passengers; however, this tour has a capacity of 125 participants.
